items.description: Analyze repository structure and available infrastructure
items.acceptance_criteria: Document listing all modules (.archivara/, .opencode/, figures/, results/), their purposes, available tools (Semantic Scholar API client at .archivara/semantic_scholar.py, literature-graph-miner subagent, TypeScript tool wrapper), and programming languages present (Python, TypeScript, JSON, Markdown). Confirm no prior Bloch-constant research code exists on the current branch.

items.description: Conduct comprehensive literature search on univalent Bloch constant B_u and related constants
items.acceptance_criteria: Search Semantic Scholar, Google Scholar, arXiv, and MathSciNet for: 'univalent Bloch constant', 'schlicht Bloch constant', 'Bloch-Landau constant univalent', 'Skinner 2009 Bloch', 'Carroll Ortega-Cerda conformal welding', 'Landau constant bounds', 'extremal univalent functions conformal radius'. Collect at least 20 relevant papers. For each, record: title, authors, year, journal, DOI, and the specific bound or technique contributed. Organize results into results/literature_survey.md.
items.notes: Use Semantic Scholar tool and websearch. Delegate citation-graph mining to literature-graph-miner subagent starting from seeds: Skinner 2009 (DOI:10.1080/17476930903197199), Carroll-Ortega-Cerda 2009 (DOI:10.1016/j.matpur.2009.05.008), Bhowmik-Sen 2023 (DOI:10.4153/S0008439523000346), Baernstein-Vinson 1998.

items.description: Create and populate sources.bib with BibTeX entries for all consulted sources
items.acceptance_criteria: File sources.bib exists in repo root with valid BibTeX entries for at least 20 papers including: Bloch 1925, Ahlfors-Grunsky 1937, Rademacher 1943, Goodman 1945, Bonk 1990, Yanagihara 1995, Chen-Gauthier 1996, Baernstein-Vinson 1998, Xiong 1998, Chen-Shiba 2004, Rettinger 2008, Ortega-Cerda-Pridhnani 2008, Carroll-Ortega-Cerda 2009, Skinner 2009, Faulhuber 2019, Bhowmik-Sen 2023, Bhowmik-Sen 2024. Each entry must have author, title, journal, year, and DOI where available. Verify no BibTeX parsing errors.
items.notes: Use semantic_scholar bibtex command for each paper. Supplement with manual entries for older works (Bloch, Ahlfors-Grunsky) not in database.

items.description: Deep-dive into Skinner 2009: reconstruct the bootstrapping iteration for B_u > 0.5708858
items.acceptance_criteria: Written analysis in results/skinner_analysis.md covering: (1) the starting growth estimate |f(z)| >= B(|z|) for f in class S using the Koebe growth theorem, (2) the key lemma constructing an implicit function C(r) >= B(r) via distortion bounds, (3) the specific form of the Koebe distortion estimates used (both upper and lower), (4) how the iterative application B_0 -> B_1 -> ... -> B_n converges to yield 0.5708858, (5) explicit identification of at least 3 conservatism sources in the proof (places where tighter estimates could improve the bound), (6) the relationship between Skinner's method and the earlier approaches of Szego and Robinson.
items.notes: Fetch paper via DOI 10.1080/17476930903197199. This analysis directly informs Phase 3 strategies.

items.description: Deep-dive into Carroll-Ortega-Cerda 2009: analyze the upper bound B_u <= 0.6564 via harmonic symmetry
items.acceptance_criteria: Written analysis in results/carroll_oc_analysis.md covering: (1) the definition of the Bloch-Landau constant A (same as B_u or related?) and the precise value A <= 0.6563937, (2) the Goodman 1945 domain construction (disk minus radial slits) and its conformal radius, (3) how Fedorov's solution to the Polya-Chebotarev problem for 4 symmetric points is used, (4) the role of harmonic symmetry and conformal welding in constructing extremal domains, (5) whether A and B_u are identical or merely related, (6) assessment of whether this 0.6564 upper bound applies directly to B_u as defined in the task description.
items.notes: Delegate initial exploration to literature-graph-miner subagent. This is critical because the task description only lists the trivial upper bound B_u <= 1, but Carroll-Ortega-Cerda may give B_u <= 0.6564.

items.description: Map the full landscape of related constants with all known bounds and techniques
items.acceptance_criteria: Structured comparison table in results/constants_landscape.json and results/constants_landscape.md with columns: constant name, symbol, definition, best lower bound, lower bound reference, best upper bound, upper bound reference, conjectured value (if any), key technique. Must cover: B (Bloch), B_l (locally univalent Bloch), L (Landau), B_u (univalent Bloch), A (Bloch-Landau/Carroll-OC). Must cite at least 12 entries from sources.bib. Must include the chain B <= B_l <= L <= B_u and note where each inequality is known to be strict.

items.description: Implement numerical computation of conformal radius and B_f for univalent functions
items.acceptance_criteria: Python module bloch_computation.py with functions: (1) conformal_radius(f, w0) computing the conformal radius of f(D) at a point w0 using the inverse mapping derivative, (2) compute_Bf(f, N_grid) computing B_f as the supremum of conformal radii over f(D) via boundary analysis on an N_grid-point mesh, (3) validate on f(z)=z (B_f=1 exactly), f(z)=z/(1-z)^2 Koebe function (B_f=1/4 analytically since it maps to C minus (-inf,-1/4]), and f(z)=z/(1-z) (B_f computable). All validations pass to 4 decimal places. Uses mpmath for arbitrary precision.
items.notes: Key insight: B_f = sup_{w in f(D)} r(f(D), w) where r(Omega, w) is the conformal radius. For simply connected domains, r(Omega, w) = |g'(0)| where g maps D onto Omega with g(0)=w.

items.description: Reproduce Skinner's iterative lower bound computation numerically
items.acceptance_criteria: Python script skinner_baseline.py that: (1) implements B_0(r) = r/(1+r)^2 (Koebe growth lower bound for class S), (2) implements the Koebe distortion bounds |f'(z)| >= (1-|z|)/(1+|z|)^3 and |f'(z)| <= (1+|z|)/(1-|z|)^3, (3) implements the iterative map B_{n+1}(r) from B_n(r) as described in Skinner 2009, (4) runs at least 20 iterations on a grid of 10000 points in [0,1), (5) extracts the lower bound for B_u from the iterated B_n, (6) reproduces a value >= 0.5708858 within numerical tolerance 1e-7. Output saved to results/skinner_baseline.json with the sequence of bounds B_0, B_1, ..., B_n at each iteration.
items.notes: If we cannot reproduce 0.5708858, document exactly where the discrepancy arises before proceeding to Phase 3.

items.description: Implement parametrized families of univalent functions for computational upper-bound search on B_u
items.acceptance_criteria: Python module univalent_families.py implementing at least 4 families: (1) rotated Koebe functions z/(1-e^{itheta}z)^2 for theta in [0,2pi), (2) one-slit mappings to C minus a ray from a point on the negative real axis, (3) starlike functions f(z)=z*exp(integral of p(e^{it}) kernel) with various p, (4) convex functions with free parameters. Each family must: verify univalence via the Noshiro-Warschawski theorem (Re f'(z) > 0) or argument principle, compute B_f numerically. A parameter sweep producing at least 500 function evaluations. Minimum B_f found saved to results/upper_bound_sweep.json.
items.notes: The minimum B_f over all univalent f with f'(0)=1 gives an upper bound for B_u. Compare with Carroll-Ortega-Cerda's 0.6564 if applicable.

items.description: Build testing framework validating all numerical modules
items.acceptance_criteria: Test file tests/test_bloch.py with at least 12 unit tests: (1) B_f for identity function = 1, (2) B_f for Koebe function = 1/4, (3) conformal radius of disk of radius R at center = R, (4) conformal radius of half-plane at a point, (5) Skinner iteration monotonicity (B_{n+1} >= B_n pointwise), (6) Skinner iteration convergence (|B_n - B_{n-1}| decreasing), (7) univalence verification for known univalent functions, (8) univalence rejection for known non-univalent functions (e.g. z^2), (9) numerical stability at r=0 and r near 1, (10) Koebe distortion bounds correctness, (11) parametrized family B_f values are positive, (12) rotational invariance (B_f same for all rotated Koebe functions). All tests pass with pytest.
items.notes: Delegate initial test skeleton creation to researcher agent, then refine.

items.description: Implement Goodman-type slit domain construction and compute its conformal radius
items.acceptance_criteria: Python module goodman_domains.py that: (1) constructs conformal maps from D onto D minus n symmetric radial slits of length l extending inward from the boundary, (2) computes the conformal radius at the origin for each configuration, (3) sweeps over n in {2,3,4,5,6,8} and slit length l in [0.01, 0.99] with at least 100 values of l per n, (4) records the minimum conformal radius found (this gives an upper bound on B_u). Results saved to results/goodman_slit_sweep.json. Compare against the Carroll-Ortega-Cerda value 0.6564.
items.notes: Goodman (1945) first suggested these domains. Carroll-Ortega-Cerda (2009) refined the construction. The n=4 case with optimal slit length should approach 0.6564.

items.description: Tighten Skinner's lower bound via refined distortion estimates and higher-order coefficient information
items.acceptance_criteria: Implement at least 4 refinement strategies in refined_lower_bound.py: (1) Replace the basic Koebe distortion bounds with sharper two-point distortion inequalities (e.g., Kim-Minda or Ma-Minda distortion theorems for subclasses of S), (2) incorporate the de Branges theorem |a_n| <= n to constrain higher-order Taylor coefficients in the iteration, (3) use the Fekete-Szego inequality |a_3 - lambda*a_2^2| bounds to get sharper initial estimates, (4) exploit the Grunsky matrix inequalities (truncated to order N) as additional constraints in each iteration step. For each strategy: run the modified iteration, record the resulting lower bound, and compare against 0.5708858. At least one strategy must produce a bound strictly greater than 0.5708858 (even by 1e-7). All results in results/refined_lower_bounds.json with per-strategy breakdown.
items.notes: Primary avenue for improving the lower bound. The key insight is that Skinner uses only the basic Koebe growth/distortion theorem, which is sharp for the full class S but not sharp when we also know higher-order coefficient constraints.

items.description: Formulate B_u lower bound as a semidefinite program over truncated Grunsky matrices
items.acceptance_criteria: Python module sdp_lower_bound.py that: (1) formulates the problem: minimize B_f over f in S subject to Grunsky matrix conditions (the Grunsky matrix G = (c_{mn}) satisfies ||G|| <= 1 as an operator on l^2), (2) truncates to finite N x N Grunsky matrices (N = 5, 10, 20, 30, 50), (3) expresses the B_f lower bound in terms of the Grunsky coefficients, (4) solves the SDP relaxation using cvxpy with SCS or MOSEK solver, (5) extracts a lower bound for B_u from the optimal value. The SDP must be mathematically justified: document why any feasible dual solution provides a valid lower bound. Record bounds for each truncation order N in results/sdp_bounds.json. The bound at N=50 should be competitive with or exceed 0.5708858.
items.notes: Delegate feasibility study and SDP formulation derivation to researcher agent. The Grunsky inequalities are necessary and sufficient for univalence (Grunsky's theorem), making this a tight relaxation as N -> infinity.

items.description: Construct near-extremal domains for tighter upper bound via numerical conformal mapping optimization
items.acceptance_criteria: Python module extremal_domain_search.py that: (1) parametrizes simply connected domains Omega containing the origin with inner radius 1 (conformal radius at origin = 1, ensuring f'(0)=1 for the Riemann map), (2) for each Omega, computes B_f = sup_w r(Omega, w) numerically, (3) searches for Omega minimizing B_f using at least 3 domain families: (a) D minus symmetric arcs (Carroll-Ortega-Cerda type), (b) D minus radial slits (Goodman type), (c) D minus thin corridors/bottlenecks, (d) domains with fractal-like boundary perturbations, (4) uses scipy.optimize or evolutionary optimization (CMA-ES) over domain parameters, (5) produces the best upper bound found for B_u. Target: B_u <= 0.66 or better. Results in results/upper_bound_optimization.json. Best domain visualized in figures/best_extremal_domain.png.
items.notes: The key constraint is that f must be a conformal map D -> Omega with f'(0) = 1, so Omega must have conformal radius 1 at f(0). We want to minimize the largest schlicht disk that fits in Omega.

items.description: Investigate Loewner chain / driving function approach to systematically generate candidate extremal functions
items.acceptance_criteria: Python module loewner_exploration.py that: (1) implements the radial Loewner equation df/dt = z * (p(z,t) + z)/(p(z,t) - z) * df/dz with various driving functions p, (2) generates univalent functions by solving the Loewner ODE from t=0 to t=T for at least 50 different driving function choices (piecewise constant, sinusoidal, step functions), (3) normalizes each to f'(0) = 1, (4) computes B_f for each, (5) identifies the driving function that produces the smallest B_f. Results in results/loewner_search.json. This approach is novel because the Loewner representation parametrizes ALL of class S, so the search is in principle complete.
items.notes: Delegate literature search on computational Loewner chain methods to literature-graph-miner subagent. Key references: Loewner 1923, Schramm 2000 (SLE), Marshall-Rohde 2005 (numerical Loewner).

items.description: Develop hybrid analytical-numerical bound: combine Skinner iteration with SDP dual certificates
items.acceptance_criteria: Implement in hybrid_bound.py: (1) use the SDP dual solution from item_013 to extract an improved starting function B_0(r) that incorporates coefficient constraints up to order N, (2) feed this improved B_0 into Skinner's iteration scheme from item_008, (3) run the combined iteration and extract the resulting lower bound, (4) verify that the hybrid bound exceeds both the pure Skinner bound (0.5708858) and the pure SDP bound from item_013. The improvement must be strictly positive. Document the mathematical justification for why the hybrid approach is valid (i.e., the combined bound is still a rigorous lower bound). Results in results/hybrid_bound.json.
items.notes: This is the most promising route to a genuinely new lower bound. Skinner's iteration is good at propagating local information; the SDP captures global coefficient constraints.

items.description: Explore probabilistic estimates via Brownian motion exit times and Monte Carlo conformal radius estimation
items.acceptance_criteria: Python module brownian_estimates.py that: (1) simulates Brownian motion starting at w in a simply connected domain Omega, (2) estimates the conformal radius r(Omega, w) via the mean exit time relation r(Omega, w)^2 = 2 * E[tau_w] where tau_w is the exit time, (3) for candidate near-extremal domains from items 011 and 014, estimates B_f = sup_w r(Omega, w) via Monte Carlo with at least 10^5 paths per starting point, (4) reports estimates with 95% confidence intervals, (5) compares Monte Carlo estimates against deterministic conformal radius computations for validation. Results in results/brownian_estimates.json. At least one figure showing convergence of estimates as sample size increases saved to figures/mc_convergence.png.
items.notes: Non-rigorous but provides independent numerical validation and may reveal structure of extremal domains.

items.description: Systematic convergence study of the refined Skinner iteration across truncation orders and grid resolutions
items.acceptance_criteria: Run the refined iterations from item_012 with: (1) coefficient truncation orders N in {5, 10, 20, 50, 100, 200}, (2) radial grid resolutions in {1000, 5000, 10000, 50000}, (3) iteration counts in {10, 20, 50, 100, 200}. Record the lower bound at each (N, grid, iterations) triple. Produce: (a) convergence-in-N plot (figures/convergence_truncation_order.png), (b) convergence-in-grid plot (figures/convergence_grid_resolution.png), (c) convergence-in-iterations plot (figures/convergence_iterations.png). Identify the configuration yielding the best lower bound. Results in results/convergence_study.json.

items.description: Systematic upper-bound search over domain parameter spaces with evolutionary optimization
items.acceptance_criteria: Run the domain optimization from items 011 and 014 with: (1) at least 6 domain families (symmetric slits with n=2,3,4,5,6 arms, arc-removed domains, corridor domains, multi-slit domains with varying angles), (2) at least 2000 total parameter configurations across all families (use CMA-ES or differential evolution), (3) numerical verification of univalence and normalization f'(0)=1 for each candidate. Record: minimum B_f found, corresponding domain parameters, domain type. Results in results/upper_bound_search.json. Best 3 domains visualized in figures/top3_extremal_domains.png.
items.notes: Delegate parallel optimization runs to researcher agent for efficiency.

items.description: Rigorous verification of the best new lower bound using interval arithmetic
items.acceptance_criteria: If a lower bound exceeding 0.5708858 was found: (1) re-implement the critical computation using mpmath with interval arithmetic (mpmath.iv module) at precision of at least 50 decimal digits, (2) verify that all inequalities in the proof chain hold with controlled rounding (every floating-point operation enclosed in a rigorous interval), (3) produce a machine-checkable certificate in results/rigorous_certificate.json listing: the claimed bound, every intermediate inequality with interval-arithmetic bounds, and the final conclusion B_u > [new value], (4) the certified bound must be strictly greater than 0.5708858. If no improvement was found, document exactly which step is the bottleneck and the best rigorous bound achievable.
items.notes: Use mpmath.iv (interval arithmetic) or python-flint. A rigorous improvement, even to B_u > 0.5708859, would be the first progress in 17 years.

items.description: Compare all bounds against prior work from the literature review
items.acceptance_criteria: Produce results/comparison_with_literature.md containing: (1) table comparing our best lower bound vs. Skinner 2009 (0.5708858) and Yanagihara 1995 (0.5 + 10^{-335}), (2) table comparing our best upper bound vs. trivial (1) and Carroll-Ortega-Cerda 2009 (0.6564 if applicable), (3) comparison of our techniques vs. prior techniques (Koebe distortion, bootstrapping, Polya-Chebotarev, conformal welding), (4) assessment of whether our improvements close a meaningful fraction of the gap, (5) explicit comparison with any post-2009 papers found in Phase 1. Must cite at least 10 entries from sources.bib.
items.notes: Delegate cross-referencing and synthesis to researcher agent.

items.description: Sensitivity and robustness analysis of all numerical methods
items.acceptance_criteria: For each method (Skinner iteration, SDP relaxation, hybrid bound, domain optimization, Monte Carlo): (1) test sensitivity to numerical parameters (precision, grid size, solver tolerances), (2) report the number of reliable decimal digits in each output, (3) identify failure modes (e.g., ill-conditioning of Grunsky matrices at high N). At least 3 convergence/stability plots saved to figures/. Summary table in results/numerical_robustness.json.

items.description: Write main results document synthesizing all findings
items.acceptance_criteria: File results/main_results.md containing: (1) precise statement of the problem and all known bounds (both before and after this work), (2) our new lower bound for B_u with the method that produced it, (3) our new upper bound for B_u (if improved beyond trivial), (4) the narrowed interval [new_lower, new_upper] for B_u, (5) description of each method attempted with success/failure assessment, (6) comparison with all prior work from literature review, (7) significance statement (how many years since last improvement, fraction of gap closed). At least 2500 words. Must cite at least 15 entries from sources.bib.

items.description: Document rigorous proof sketches for all claimed bounds
items.acceptance_criteria: File results/proof_sketches.md containing: for each rigorous bound claimed: (1) complete proof sketch that a complex analyst could verify in detail, (2) explicit statement of which theorems from the literature are invoked (with citations to sources.bib), (3) clear separation between rigorous steps and numerical approximations, (4) reference to specific code files, functions, and line numbers that implement each step, (5) discussion of what would be needed to upgrade numerical estimates to fully rigorous proofs. Must be self-contained for independent verification.

items.description: Generate comprehensive visualization suite
items.acceptance_criteria: At least 6 figures in figures/ directory: (1) lower_bound_convergence.png - convergence of iterative lower bounds across methods, (2) upper_bound_landscape.png - heatmap of B_f over domain parameter spaces, (3) extremal_domain.png - visualization of the domain(s) giving smallest B_f found, (4) constants_chain.png - visual comparison of B, B_l, L, B_u with old and new bounds shown as intervals, (5) method_comparison.png - bar chart comparing bounds from each approach, (6) sdp_scaling.png - how the SDP bound improves with truncation order N. All figures have proper axis labels, titles, legends, and are publication-quality (300 DPI, vector format where possible).

items.description: Update sources.bib with all additional references discovered during Phases 2-4
items.acceptance_criteria: sources.bib contains valid BibTeX entries for every paper cited anywhere in results/ or referenced in code comments. Total count must be at least 25 entries. Verify all entries parse correctly (run a BibTeX validator or check manually). New additions beyond Phase 1 must include any papers on: Loewner chains, SDP methods in geometric function theory, numerical conformal mapping, Brownian motion and conformal invariance.

items.description: Final summary: state best bounds achieved, assess novelty, and identify open directions
items.acceptance_criteria: File results/final_summary.md containing: (1) the single best lower bound achieved with whether it is rigorous or numerical-only, (2) the single best upper bound achieved with whether it is rigorous or numerical-only, (3) the narrowed interval for B_u compared to the pre-existing [0.5708858, 1] (or [0.5708858, 0.6564] if Carroll-OC applies), (4) explicit yes/no answer: was B_u > 0.5708858 achieved rigorously?, (5) ranked list of the top 5 most promising approaches for future work with specific next steps, (6) an honest failure analysis: which approaches did not yield improvements and why, (7) assessment of feasibility of closing the remaining gap to the conjectured value (if one exists). At most 1500 words, concise and direct.
